title: Triage campaign: 2 of 15 ARC-AGI-2 public-eval tasks with audited give-ups
goal: Get at least two of the fifteen sealed ARC-AGI-2 public-evaluation tasks in assets/gc-448/task_ids.txt fully solved while running an audited portfolio: a standing triage table at runs/gc-448/triage.md ranks all fifteen by estimated tractability and is re-scored after every work session, and any task abandoned must carry a written give-up rationale naming the rule families tried and the specific train pair each one failed. Budget discipline is part of the goal -- the ledger must show that most spend went to the top-ranked tractable tasks rather than being spread evenly, and that at least one near-miss got a second campaign after the initial failure.
resources: github repo: arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 pinned at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49 (task JSONs under data/training/ and data/evaluation/; each task file holds train pairs plus one or more test pairs)
assets/gc-448/task_ids.txt (sealed list of 15 task ids, one per line; all from the public evaluation split; every id verified to exist in the pinned commit)
assets/gc-448/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: downloads the gold task files for the pinned commit, scores predictions cell-exactly, and prints {"solved": N} as its last JSON line)

output convention: runs/gc-448/predictions.json mapping task_id -> list with one entry per test input; each entry is a grid, a list of at most two attempt grids, or {"attempt_1": grid, "attempt_2": grid}
network: raw.githubusercontent.com must be reachable at grade time (the grader caches gold files under runs/gc-448/gold_cache/)
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-448/plan.md before the first prediction is written, naming per-task priorities, the attempt budget, and the exact verification command.

Every predicted task has a written transformation-rule hypothesis that was checked against every train pair before the test prediction; tasks where a hypothesis failed a train pair are logged by id with the revision that fixed it.
The grader was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.
The gold test outputs inside the pinned public repo are off-limits as inputs: predictions must be derived from the train pairs alone, and the run log must show that derivation per task.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-448/ledger.json records per-task attempts, spend, and outcome, including abandoned tasks and failed grader runs.
runs/gc-448/triage.md is re-scored after every work session, and every abandoned task carries a give-up rationale naming the rule families tried and the train pair each failed on.
